walkthroughs.body_html:
Waves erode coasts in four main ways.

Hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution.

Each attacks the cliff in a different way.

Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast.

Swash rolls beach material up at the prevailing wind angle.

Backwash pulls it straight back down the slope. Repeat — zig-zag transport!

Two wave types matter.

Constructive waves are low and gentle, with strong swash that builds beaches.

Destructive waves are tall and steep, with strong backwash that erodes.

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
The zigzag movement of sediment along a coast caused by waves approaching at an angle (swash up the beach) and gravity returning water perpendicular (backwash).
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Sand moves along the beach because tides pull it sideways.
A spit is a small island just off the coast.
A spit forms where the river deposits its sediment at the coast.
Longshore drift carries sediment past a change in coastline direction (e.g. river mouth); deposition continues into deeper water, building a curved depositional landform with a hook.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
